title: The Production Web Server
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of the production web server and at least two listed subtopics.
Interpret the the production web server example and predict its expected result.
Choose a verification step and identify one version, security, data, or troubleshooting consideration.

content.intro: Learn the production web server through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: The Production Web Server matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines the production web server as part of deployment and production operations. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Application-server concepts; WSGI and ASGI servers; Reverse proxies; Worker configuration; Health checks and graceful restarts. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Application-server concepts
items.text: Application-server concepts should be planned for the actual hosting topology: configuration, permissions, resource limits, observability, rollback/recovery and a testable operating procedure all matter.

items.title: WSGI and ASGI servers
items.text: WSGI is the traditional synchronous Python web-server interface. Verify server and middleware compatibility before choosing it for a workload.

items.title: Reverse proxies
items.text: For Reverse proxies, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Worker configuration
items.text: Configuration for Worker configuration should be explicit, environment-aware, and validated before serving requests. Record defaults and deploy-specific values, keep secrets outside committed content, and test the setting that changes behavior.

items.title: Health checks and graceful restarts
items.text: Treat Health checks and graceful restarts as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: The Production Web Server
content_blocks.expected_output: An async view can await an async-capable client and return a response.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: The client is illustrative. Use compatible non-blocking libraries, timeouts, bounded concurrency and the documented sync/async boundaries; transactions need special care.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First identify the input and the responsible Django component. Next trace how the example moves through “The Production Web Server” and the related concept “Application-server concepts”. Predict the result before running or inspecting it. Finally compare the observed behavior with the expected result and the cited official documentation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Application-server concepts. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to describe the production web server, explain the listed topics, inspect the example, and choose an appropriate verification step. Keep the scope and version caveat visible when sharing your solution.

common_mistakes.why: The snippet may be incomplete when separated from a Django project.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the stated prerequisites and run the relevant management check or focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting input or relying only on a happy-path example.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid values, unauthorized requests, or concurrent activity can violate assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and add a negative or boundary test.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating the development sample as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Production hosting, secrets, storage, monitoring and resource limits differ from local use.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the current deployment/security references and document untested areas.
